definition.title: Rocket / Mission Designer
learning_objectives: Relate stage mass ratio and specific impulse to ideal rocket-equation delta-v.
Follow explicit serial-stage mass bookkeeping through propellant burn and dry-stage jettison.
Compare thrust with a fixed selected-body surface-weight reference without treating it as an in-flight trajectory model.
Explore how payload changes ideal staged delta-v while keeping the submitted stages fixed.
Compare ideal vehicle delta-v with cited educational velocity references without turning the comparison into a mission-feasibility verdict.

fields.name: stages
fields.meaning: One through four serial stages in ignition order. Each supplies dry mass, propellant mass, specific impulse, and thrust.

input_schema.relational_guard: Submitted payload plus all stage wet masses must not exceed 10000000 kg.
input_schema.invalid_handling: Reject booleans, non-finite values, unknown closed identifiers, out-of-range values, non-tuples, non-stage records, stage counts outside 1..4, and launch masses above the reviewed guard. No input is silently clamped, reordered, merged, or optimized.

output_schema: per-stage ignition mass and burnout-before-jettison mass
per-stage mass ratio, effective exhaust velocity, and ideal rocket-equation delta-v
stage and whole-vehicle descriptive mass fractions
one fixed educational velocity-reference comparison with explicit non-feasibility language

equations.ideal_rocket_equation: delta_v = Isp * g0 * ln(m0/m1), with g0 = 9.80665 m/s^2
equations.stage_initial_mass: m0 is the current stage wet mass plus every later stage wet mass plus payload
equations.stage_final_mass: m1 is m0 minus only the current stage propellant mass; current dry mass is jettisoned only after that stage delta-v is evaluated
equations.total_ideal_delta_v: sum of the per-stage ideal delta-v values
equations.payload_sensitivity: Re-evaluate the unchanged stage stack at payload multipliers 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, and 2

definition.default_preset: Synthetic unnamed two-stage teaching vehicle: Earth surface-gravity reference, NASA Glenn 200-mile orbit educational comparison, 5000 kg payload; stage 1 = 30000 kg dry, 400000 kg propellant, 300 s Isp, 7000000 N thrust; stage 2 = 8000 kg dry, 40000 kg propellant, 350 s Isp, 1000000 N thrust.
assumptions: The ideal rocket equation is applied with no external-force losses inside each stage calculation.
Stages burn sequentially in submitted order; a spent stage's dry mass is removed before the next stage ignites.
Specific impulse uses conventional exact standard gravity g0, independent of the selected gravity body.
The selected gravity body is used only for a constant surface-gravity thrust-to-weight teaching reference.
Payload sensitivity keeps every submitted stage property fixed and changes payload mass only.
Fixed comparison values are educational velocity references; they are not complete mission requirements.
limitations: No atmospheric drag, gravity loss, steering loss, changing gravity with altitude, Earth rotation, finite-burn trajectory integration, or launch-site geometry.
No pressure-dependent specific impulse, throttle, engine-out behavior, nozzle/combustion design, propellant chemistry, tankage, or structural sizing.
No aerodynamic load, heating, staging transient, guidance/navigation/control, reliability, reserve, margin, cost, or uncertainty model.
No orbital insertion, Hohmann/interplanetary transfer design, landing, ascent guidance, reentry, or operational launch procedure.
Surface-gravity TWR is not an upper-stage in-flight acceleration estimate.
A positive difference from a fixed reference does not establish mission capability; a negative difference does not establish impossibility.
The payload sensitivity table is not an optimizer or design recommendation.
The model provides no hazardous construction instructions.

validation_fixtures.purpose: A simple one-stage case reproduces Isp*g0*ln(m0/m1) exactly within floating-point tolerance.
Stage two ignition mass excludes stage-one propellant and spent stage-one dry mass while retaining later stage mass and payload.
Changing the selected gravity body leaves ideal delta-v unchanged because specific impulse always uses exact conventional g0.
The same stage stack produces different surface-gravity TWR references for Earth and Mars while preserving identical rocket-equation delta-v.
Stage dry, propellant, and payload fractions close the submitted launch-mass partition.
For fixed positive stage masses and Isp, the five reviewed increasing payload samples produce a non-increasing total ideal delta-v sequence and the 1x point equals the canonical result.
All three fixed comparison references reproduce their reviewed values and preserve explicit non-feasibility language.
Bool, non-finite, and out-of-range stage mass, Isp, and thrust inputs fail closed.
Unknown gravity/reference IDs, invalid payloads, invalid containers, and stage-count violations fail closed.
A submitted stage stack above the reviewed 10000000 kg launch-mass guard is rejected rather than evaluated.
Identical canonical inputs produce exactly identical immutable results.
Source, constant, gravity-body, comparison-reference, preset, fixture, and model-version drift is rejected by the strict artifact loader.

scientific_validation.method: Cross-check ideal rocket-equation output against the NASA Glenn/NASA-JPL form using exact NIST g0; verify explicit multi-stage mass bookkeeping, selected-body surface-gravity TWR references, fraction closure, payload sensitivity, fixed comparison references, deterministic behavior, numeric/domain guards, and strict artifact integrity.

tools.name: pytest
tools.role: Analytic source-reference, staging, boundary, deterministic, domain, and artifact-integrity regression tests.
